milwaukee_history.fact: The annual Riverside run began in 2006 with a single Saturday show that sold out quickly. Panic was one of the first acts booked after Pabst Theater Group took over the Riverside. (Relix/jambands say 'most years since 2008' instead, so the start year differs by source.)
Then-Mayor Tom Barrett declared Thursday, Oct. 21, 2021 'Widespread Panic Day' in Milwaukee.

Oct. 2016 'Sabbath run': a Black Sabbath cover every night, with Fairies Wear Boots on Friday, Sweet Leaf as Saturday's encore (10/22/16), and Children of the Grave as Sunday's encore (10/23/16). Children of the Grave had not been played since 10/31/07, a 604-show gap.

Closing night 10/26/25 ended with a double encore: Cosmic Confidante, Soul Kitchen (The Doors, only the 4th time ever and a 52-show gap), Postcard, then Love Tractor. The show also brought back A of D (84-show gap) and Dirty Business.

The archival release 'Milwaukee, WI 1996' (Porch Songs series, out 2010) captures the 11/1/96 show at the Modjeska Theatre with Michael Houser. It includes the first time the band covered Sick and Tired and Shake, Rattle and Roll.

reviews.title: Widespread Panic Tips Its Cap to World Series With First-Ever "Rebirtha" Opener in Milwaukee
reviews.author: James Sissler
reviews.summary: Night 1 opened with Rebirtha for the first time ever as a nod to the Brewers' World Series, with Nick Johnson covering for Jimmy Herring and a Herring Brewers jersey hung onstage.
